page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors. The instance delivers 96 physical cores across 96 dedicated vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core configuration. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core characteristic of compute-focused platforms. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present on this machine type.

Integrated directly into the instance is 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-capacity, low-latency temporary block storage. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 50 Gbps, enabling efficient data transfer for distributed systems and storage synchronization. Public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary with the configuration and require explicit allocation.

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation eliminates hyper-threading contention, delivering consistent per-core execution for heavily parallel tasks. Paired with substantial local NVMe storage and high baseline network bandwidth, the instance offers strong resource density and qualitative operational efficiency for compute-heavy applications that process large scratch datasets locally. Workloads must support the arm64 architecture, and applications requiring memory ratios above 2 GB per core or persistent root storage natively on local disks will need appropriate architectural accommodations.

Appropriate deployments include continuous integration and build systems, video encoding pipelines, batch data processing, high-performance computing clusters, distributed database nodes requiring fast scratch storage, and web application servers handling heavy parallel request volumes.
